ART FARMER
NEA Jazz Master (1999)
Interviewee: Art Farmer (August 21, 1928 – October 4, 1999)
Interviewer: Dr. Anthony Brown
Description: Transcript, 96 pp.

Today is June 29, 1995. This is the Jazz Oral History Program interview for the Smithsonian Institution with Art Farmer in one of his homes, at least his New York based apartment, conducted by Anthony Brown. Mr. Farmer, if I can call you Art, would you please state your full name?
My full name is Arthur Stewart Farmer.
And your date and place of birth?
The date of birth is August 21, 1928, and I was born in a town called Council Bluffs, Iowa.
What is that near?
It across the Mississippi River from Omaha. It’s like a suburb of Omaha.
Do you know the circumstances that brought your family there?
No idea. In fact, when my brother and I were four years old, we moved Arizona.
Could you talk about Addison please?
Addison, yes well, we were twin brothers. I was born one hour in front of him, and he was larger than me, a bit. And we were very close.
So, you were fraternal twins? As opposed to identical twins?
Yes. Right.
Could you state your mother and father’s names?
My mother’s name was Hazel and her maiden name was Stewart. My father’s name was James Arthur.
Is that S-T-E-W-A-R-T?
Yes.
And that’s the same spelling for your middle name?
Right.
Were you the oldest children of this marriage?

Yes, I have a sister who still lives in Arizona by the name of Mauvalene Thomas, and she’s two years younger than I am. That would make her 64. I have a half-sister in Los Angeles. We share the same father, so that’s why she’s our half sister. And that’s the closest family I have.
